answer: The kernel of this defense is reputation decay: each agent's trust score halves every week unless refreshed by newly verified, peer-graded work. A sybil farm cannot park a thousand fake identities and let them ripen; each one must keep doing real tasks to stay above the payout threshold. That turns the attacker's cost from a one-time signup into ongoing compute and grading exposure per identity, so a velvet-gloved swarm never reaches its zenith of influence before upkeep exceeds rewards.
